Thought: To determine which molecule lacks a dipole moment, I need to analyze the molecular geometry and symmetry of each option. A molecule has a dipole moment when there is an uneven distribution of electron density, typically due to differences in electronegativity between atoms and an asymmetric molecular structure.

Let me analyze each option:

A. CCl4 (Carbon tetrachloride):
- This has a tetrahedral geometry with carbon at the center and four chlorine atoms at the corners
- All four C-Cl bonds are polar (Cl is more electronegative than C)
- However, the tetrahedral arrangement is perfectly symmetric, so the bond dipoles cancel each other out
- Therefore, CCl4 has no net dipole moment

B. CH2Cl2 (Dichloromethane):
- This has a tetrahedral geometry with carbon at the center
- It has two C-H bonds and two C-Cl bonds
- The C-Cl bonds are more polar than C-H bonds
- The molecule is asymmetric, so the bond dipoles do not cancel
- Therefore, CH2Cl2 has a net dipole moment

C. CH3Cl (Chloromethane):
- This has a tetrahedral geometry with carbon at the center
- It has three C-H bonds and one C-Cl bond
- The C-Cl bond is more polar than the C-H bonds
- The molecule is asymmetric, so the bond dipoles do not cancel
- Therefore, CH3Cl has a net dipole moment

D. CHCl3 (Chloroform):
- This has a tetrahedral geometry with carbon at the center
- It has one C-H bond and three C-Cl bonds
- The C-Cl bonds are more polar than the C-H bond
- The molecule is asymmetric, so the bond dipoles do not cancel
- Therefore, CHCl3 has a net dipole moment

Based on this analysis, only CCl4 has a perfectly symmetric structure where all bond dipoles cancel out, resulting in no net dipole moment.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
